XXVIII.}}</noinclude>was forsaken, for two causes, first because it was the wil of God not to deliuer him, but that he should die: secondly, because his diuine nature did so represse it self for the time, that he felt no comfort thereof at al, but was left to die in extreme paines as a mere man.

''59. Wrapped.''] {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Reuerent vsing of our L. Body.}}This honour and duty done to Christes body being dead, was maruelous grateful and meritorious. And this wrapping of it in cleane sindon may signifie by S. Hierom, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''S. Hiero. in hunc locum.''}}that the Body of our Lord is to be wrapped not in gold, pretious stones, and silke, but in pure linnen. And so in the whole Church it is obserued by {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=* ''to. 1, Cōcil''.}}* S. Siluesters constitution, that the Corporal {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=Corporals.}}whereupon our Lordes body lieth on the altar, must be pure and plaine linnen.

{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XXVIII.}}}}}}

{{c|''He riseth againe the third day, and (the blind most obstinate Iewes by bribery working to their owne reprobation) he appeareth to his Disciples in Galilee (as both before his Passion he foretold them Mat. 26, and now after his Resurrection, first the Angel, then also him self appointed by the women) 18 and sendeth them to al Nations, to build his Church among ehe Gentils.''}} {{verse|chapter=28|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The Gospel for the night Masse of Christes Resurrection, which is now vsed to be said on Easter eue in the morning.}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=EASTER day.}}AND in the euening of the Sabboth vvhich davvneth on the first of the Sabboth, came Marie Magdalene, and the other Marie ‖ to see the sepulchre.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 16, 1. Luc. 24, 1. Io. 20, 1.''}} {{verse|chapter=28|verse=2}}† And behold there vvas made a great earth-quake. For an Angel of our Lord descended from heauen: and comming, rolled backe the stone, and sate vpon it: {{verse|chapter=28|verse=3}}† and his countenance vvas as lightening: and his garment as snovv. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=4}}† And for feare of him, the vvatchmen vvere frighted, and became as dead. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=5}}† And the Angel ansvvering said to the vvomen, Feare not you. for I know that you seeke IESVS that vvas crucified. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=6}}† he is not here: for he is risen, {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 26, 32.''}}* as he said. come, and see the place vvhere our Lord vvas laid. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=7}}† And going quickly, tel ye his Disciples that he is risen: and behold he goeth before you into Galilee. there you shal see him. loe I haue fortold you.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=8}}† And they vvent forth quickly out of the monument vvith feare and great ioy, running to tel his Disciples. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=9}}† And behold IESVS mette them, saying, Al haile. But they came neere and tooke hold of his feete, and adored him. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=10}}† Then IESVS said to them, Feare not. goe, tel my brethren that they goe into Galilee, there they shal see me.

{{verse|chapter=28|verse=11}}† Who vvhen they vvere departed, behold certaine of the vvatchmen came into the citie, and told the cheefe Priestes al things that had been done. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=12}}† And being assembled together vvith the auncients, taking counsel, they gaue a greate summe of money to the souldiars, {{verse|chapter=28|verse=13}}† saying, Say you, That his Disciples came by night, and stole him avvay vvhen vve were a sleepe. {{verse|chapter=28|verse=14}}† And if the President shal heare of this, vve<noinclude>{{rh|||vvil}}</noinclude>
